title: Bees on the rooftops
paragraphs: Ten years ago, very few city dwellers would have {taken} up beekeeping as a hobby. Today, however, hives have become a familiar {sight} on the roofs of offices, hotels and even schools. The trend {gathered} pace when the public became increasingly {aware} of the dramatic fall in bee populations across Europe.

Keeping bees in a city {makes} more sense than you might think. Parks and private gardens offer a wide {range} of flowers, and because pesticides are rarely used there, urban bees are often healthier than their country cousins. In {fact}, some city hives produce more honey than those in the countryside.

Not everyone is enthusiastic, though. Some experts {warn} that too many hives could harm wild bees, which have to {compete} with honeybees for food. They argue that planting more flowers would do far more {good} than adding yet another hive. Beekeepers, for their {part}, insist that the two approaches are not in conflict.

gaps.label: take up (un hobby)
gaps.explanation: TAKE UP = empezar una actividad o un hobby.

gaps.label: a familiar sight
gaps.explanation: 'a familiar/common sight' = algo que se ve seguido. VIEW es un paisaje o una opinión, no una cosa que se ve.

gaps.label: gather pace
gaps.explanation: 'gather pace' = acelerarse, tomar impulso. Es una colocación fija: no se dice COLLECT pace.

gaps.label: aware of
gaps.explanation: 'become aware OF something' = darse cuenta. ALERT va con TO, y SENSIBLE es un falso amigo: significa 'sensato'.

gaps.label: make sense
gaps.explanation: 'make sense' = tener sentido. Siempre con MAKE.

gaps.label: a wide range of
gaps.explanation: 'a wide range of' = una gran variedad de. SCALE y SCOPE hablan de tamaño o alcance, no de variedad.

gaps.label: in fact
gaps.explanation: IN FACT refuerza o amplía lo anterior con un dato. 'In case' significa 'por si acaso'.

gaps.label: warn that
gaps.explanation: WARN THAT = advertir sobre un peligro. ALERT y REMIND necesitan un objeto ('alert someone', 'remind someone').

gaps.label: compete with … for
gaps.explanation: 'compete WITH someone FOR something' = competir con alguien por algo. RIVAL es transitivo y no lleva WITH.

gaps.label: do (more) good
gaps.explanation: 'do good' = hacer bien. Va con DO, y es la frase opuesta a 'do harm'.

gaps.label: for their part
gaps.explanation: 'for my/their part' = por su parte. Es fija: no se dice 'for their side' (sería 'on their side').

title: The art of doing nothing
paragraphs: Most of us feel guilty when we spend an afternoon doing nothing at {all}. We have been taught that every minute should be used productively, so we fill our free time with exercise classes, online courses and endless household {chores}. Yet a growing number of psychologists believe that this constant activity may be doing us more {harm} than good.

According to their research, the brain does not simply switch {off} when we stop concentrating. On the {contrary}, periods of rest allow it to process memories and make connections between ideas. This may explain why so many people come {up} with their best ideas in the shower or on a long walk.

Of {course}, doing nothing is harder than it sounds. Many people find that, within minutes, they {reach} for their phones. The experts' advice is to start small: ten minutes a day without music or screens can {make} a real difference. It may feel strange at {first}, but most people soon begin to look {forward} to these quiet moments.

gaps.label: nothing at all
gaps.explanation: 'nothing at all' = absolutamente nada. AT ALL refuerza una negación.

gaps.label: household chores
gaps.explanation: CHORES son las tareas de la casa. WORK es incontable en este sentido: 'works' es otra cosa (obras, fábrica).

gaps.label: do more harm than good
gaps.explanation: 'do more harm than good' = hacer más mal que bien. Es una expresión fija con HARM.

gaps.label: switch off
gaps.explanation: SWITCH OFF = apagarse; también, desconectarse mentalmente.

gaps.label: on the contrary
gaps.explanation: ON THE CONTRARY niega lo anterior y dice lo opuesto. Con CONTRAST la frase es 'in contrast', no 'on the'.

gaps.label: come up with
gaps.explanation: COME UP WITH = ocurrírsele algo (una idea, un plan). COME ACROSS = encontrarse algo por casualidad.

gaps.label: of course
gaps.explanation: OF COURSE = por supuesto. Ninguna otra palabra entra en 'of ___' con ese sentido.

gaps.label: reach for
gaps.explanation: REACH FOR something = estirar la mano para agarrar algo. ACHIEVE y ATTAIN son 'lograr' y no llevan FOR.

gaps.label: make a difference
gaps.explanation: 'make a difference' = marcar una diferencia. Siempre con MAKE.

gaps.label: at first
gaps.explanation: AT FIRST = al principio, para contrastar con lo que pasa después. 'At the beginning' necesita THE.

gaps.label: look forward to
gaps.explanation: LOOK FORWARD TO = esperar algo con ganas. LOOK AFTER es cuidar; LOOK UP TO, admirar.

title: A second life for old clothes
paragraphs: Shoppers are finally starting to {pay} attention to the environmental cost of fashion, an industry that is {responsible} for a large share of global carbon emissions. Rather than buying new clothes every season, more and more people are {opting} for second-hand shops and online platforms where they can buy and sell used items. What was once seen as a sign of poverty has become something to be proud {of}.

Repairing clothes is also {making} a comeback. In many cities, volunteers run free workshops where people can learn to fix a torn jacket {instead} of throwing it away. Organisers say that participants {take} enormous pride in wearing something they have repaired with their own hands.

Of course, second-hand shopping is not a perfect solution. Critics {point} out that some people simply buy more because the prices are so {low}. Even so, most environmental experts {agree} that wearing what already exists is better than producing more. As one designer {put} it, the greenest garment is the one already in your wardrobe.

gaps.label: pay attention
gaps.explanation: 'pay attention to' = prestar atención. Siempre con PAY.

gaps.label: responsible for
gaps.explanation: 'be responsible FOR' = ser responsable de algo. GUILTY y ACCUSED van con OF.

gaps.label: opt for
gaps.explanation: OPT FOR = optar por. CHOOSE y SELECT son transitivos: no llevan FOR delante del objeto.

gaps.label: proud of
gaps.explanation: 'proud OF something' = orgulloso de algo. Es la preposición dependiente de PROUD.

gaps.label: make a comeback
gaps.explanation: 'make a comeback' = volver a estar de moda o en uso. Siempre con MAKE.

gaps.label: instead of
gaps.explanation: INSTEAD OF + -ing = en lugar de. RATHER va con THAN; DESPITE no lleva OF.

gaps.label: take pride in
gaps.explanation: 'take pride in something' = enorgullecerse de algo. La colocación es con TAKE.

gaps.label: point out
gaps.explanation: POINT OUT = señalar, hacer notar. 'Show out' y 'mark out' no tienen ese sentido.

gaps.label: low prices
gaps.explanation: Los precios son HIGH o LOW. 'Cheap' se usa para el producto, no para el precio.

gaps.label: agree that
gaps.explanation: AGREE THAT + oración = coincidir en algo. APPROVE va con OF, y CONSENT con TO.

gaps.label: as someone put it
gaps.explanation: 'as X put it' = como dijo X. Es una fórmula fija para citar a alguien.

title: Never too late
paragraphs: When my grandmother announced that she was going to learn to drive at the {age} of sixty-two, the whole family thought she was joking. She had always {relied} on my grandfather to take her everywhere, but after he became ill, she realised she had no choice.

Her first lessons did not go {well}. She practised every evening in an empty car park, {despite} feeling terribly nervous, but she {kept} confusing the brake with the accelerator, and once she drove straight into a hedge. Most people would have given {up} at that point, but she refused to let one bad experience put her {off}.

Six months and thirty lessons later, she {passed} her test at the first {attempt}. The examiner told her that she was one of the most careful drivers he had ever {come} across. Now she drives herself to her dance class every week and, as she likes to {remind} us, she has never had a single accident.

gaps.label: at the age of
gaps.explanation: 'at the age of + número' = a los … años.

gaps.label: rely on
gaps.explanation: RELY ON = depender de alguien. TRUST no lleva preposición; BELIEVE IN es creer en.

gaps.label: go well
gaps.explanation: Después de GO hace falta un adverbio: 'go well'. GOOD es un adjetivo.

gaps.label: despite + -ing
gaps.explanation: DESPITE + -ing o + sustantivo = a pesar de. HOWEVER y NEVERTHELESS conectan oraciones; no van delante de un -ing.

gaps.label: keep + -ing
gaps.explanation: KEEP + -ing = seguir haciendo algo una y otra vez. STAY y REMAIN van con adjetivos, no con -ing.

gaps.label: give up
gaps.explanation: GIVE UP = rendirse, abandonar. GIVE AWAY es regalar; GIVE BACK, devolver.

gaps.label: put someone off
gaps.explanation: PUT SOMEONE OFF = quitarle las ganas a alguien. PUT AWAY es guardar; PUT BACK, devolver a su lugar.

gaps.label: pass a test
gaps.explanation: Un examen se PASS. APPROVE es falso amigo: significa 'aprobar' una propuesta, no un examen. SUCCEED va con IN.

gaps.label: at the first attempt
gaps.explanation: 'at the first attempt' = al primer intento. INTENT es intención; EFFORT, esfuerzo.

gaps.label: come across
gaps.explanation: COME ACROSS someone = encontrarse con alguien, conocer a alguien. 'Meet' no lleva ACROSS.

gaps.label: remind vs remember
gaps.explanation: REMIND SOMEONE = hacerle acordar algo a otro. REMEMBER es acordarse uno mismo y no lleva a otra persona como objeto.

title: Why we love disaster films
paragraphs: Earthquakes, alien invasions, giant waves: disaster films have been popular for decades, and they show no {sign} of going out of fashion. Critics often {dismiss} them as noisy and predictable, yet many of them {make} a fortune at the box office.

Psychologists believe that the appeal {lies} in the safety of the experience. We can {face} our worst fears from the comfort of a cinema seat, knowing that nothing can actually harm us. Experts {refer} to this as 'safe fear'. In this {sense}, watching a disaster film is a kind of rehearsal for real life.

These films also {tend} to celebrate ordinary people. The heroes are rarely superheroes but teachers, nurses and bus drivers who {rise} to the challenge, and they {remind} us of what really matters. In the {end}, the family is reunited and the city is rebuilt, which is perhaps the most comforting message of all.

gaps.label: show no sign of
gaps.explanation: 'show no sign of + -ing' = no dar señales de algo.

gaps.label: dismiss as
gaps.explanation: DISMISS something AS … = descartarlo por considerarlo algo. Solo DISMISS admite la estructura con AS.

gaps.label: make a fortune
gaps.explanation: 'make a fortune' = hacer una fortuna. Con plata, la colocación es MAKE: make money, make a profit.

gaps.label: lie in
gaps.explanation: 'the appeal/problem lies IN …' = el atractivo está en… Es el verbo LIE (estar, residir).

gaps.label: face your fears
gaps.explanation: FACE a fear = enfrentar un miedo. FRONT no es verbo en este sentido; OPPOSE es oponerse a una idea.

gaps.label: refer to … as
gaps.explanation: REFER TO something AS … = llamar a algo de cierta forma. CALL y NAME no llevan TO: 'call this safe fear'.

gaps.label: in this sense
gaps.explanation: 'in this sense' = en este sentido. Es fija: no se dice 'in this meaning'.

gaps.label: tend to
gaps.explanation: TEND TO + infinitivo = soler, tender a. INTEND es tener intención, y una película no tiene intenciones.

gaps.label: rise to the challenge
gaps.explanation: 'rise to the challenge' = estar a la altura. RISE es intransitivo; RAISE necesita objeto: 'raise your hand'.

gaps.label: remind someone of
gaps.explanation: REMIND SOMEONE OF something = hacerle recordar algo a alguien. REMEMBER no lleva a otra persona como objeto.

gaps.label: in the end
gaps.explanation: IN THE END = al final, finalmente. 'At last' existe, pero sin THE y con otro sentido: por fin.

title: Thank goodness it's Thursday
paragraphs: When a software company in Glasgow decided to {give} its staff every Friday off, many people expected productivity to fall. Instead, the opposite happened: output rose, fewer people called in sick and the company found it far easier to {attract} new employees.

The idea is not new, but it has {gained} popularity since the pandemic, when millions of people were forced to rethink the {way} they work. Supporters argue that when staff know they only have four days, they {cut} down on pointless meetings and concentrate on what really matters. They also {point} to the benefits for family life and mental health.

However, the model does not {suit} every business. Hospitals and shops cannot simply close for an extra day, so they would need to {take} on more staff, which could {prove} expensive. The workers themselves, {on} the other hand, are almost always in favour, and the number of companies {carrying} out trials is growing every year.

gaps.label: give someone a day off
gaps.explanation: 'give someone a day off' = darle a alguien el día libre. LET y ALLOW necesitan otro verbo: 'let them have'.

gaps.label: attract employees
gaps.explanation: ATTRACT = atraer, con objeto directo. APPEAL necesita TO: 'appeal to new employees'.

gaps.label: gain popularity
gaps.explanation: 'gain popularity' = ganar popularidad. Con GROW sería 'grown IN popularity'.

gaps.label: the way they work
gaps.explanation: 'the way + oración' = la forma en que… Solo WAY entra sin preposición; con MANNER sería 'the manner in which'.

gaps.label: cut down on
gaps.explanation: CUT DOWN ON something = reducir algo. PUT DOWN, TAKE DOWN y BREAK DOWN no llevan ON.

gaps.label: point to
gaps.explanation: POINT TO something = señalar algo como prueba o argumento. SHOW no lleva TO.

gaps.label: suit
gaps.explanation: SUIT = convenirle a alguien, ser adecuado para él. MATCH es combinar con algo; AGREE va con WITH.

gaps.label: take on staff
gaps.explanation: TAKE ON = contratar gente. PUT ON es ponerse ropa; BRING ON, provocar.

gaps.label: prove + adjetivo
gaps.explanation: PROVE + adjetivo = resultar ser. RESULT va con IN: 'result in high costs'.

gaps.label: on the other hand
gaps.explanation: ON THE OTHER HAND = por otro lado. La preposición es siempre ON.

gaps.label: carry out
gaps.explanation: CARRY OUT = llevar a cabo (una prueba, un estudio, un experimento).

title: The village without cars
paragraphs: Brenno, a small village at the {foot} of a mountain in the Swiss Alps, has banned petrol cars {since} the 1970s. Today, visitors {arrive} by train and then walk, cycle or take one of the small electric taxis that move silently through the streets. Originally, the ban was introduced to {protect} the clean mountain air.

In fact, many tourists choose Brenno precisely {because} of its car-free streets, which {make} it feel like a place from another century. Children play safely outside, and the only noise at night {comes} from the river. Many visitors say it takes a day or two to get {used} to the silence.

Life without cars has its difficulties, of course. Residents who need to travel {further} afield have to keep their vehicles in a car park outside the village. Nevertheless, when locals were asked in a recent survey whether they would {bring} back cars, almost nobody was {keen} on the idea.

gaps.label: at the foot of
gaps.explanation: 'at the foot of a mountain' = al pie de una montaña.

gaps.label: since + momento
gaps.explanation: Con present perfect: SINCE + un momento ('since the 1970s'), FOR + un período ('for fifty years').

gaps.label: arrive vs reach
gaps.explanation: ARRIVE es intransitivo: 'arrive by train'. REACH necesita objeto: 'reach the village'.

gaps.label: protect
gaps.explanation: PROTECT = cuidar algo para que no se dañe. DEFEND es contra un ataque; COVER, tapar.

gaps.label: because of
gaps.explanation: BECAUSE OF + sustantivo. DUE y OWING van con TO; THANKS, también: 'thanks to'.

gaps.label: make + objeto + infinitivo
gaps.explanation: MAKE something FEEL/LOOK = hacer que algo parezca. CAUSE necesita TO: 'cause it to feel'.

gaps.label: come from
gaps.explanation: COME FROM = venir de, provenir de. ARRIVE FROM habla de personas que llegan de un viaje.

gaps.label: get used to
gaps.explanation: GET USED TO something = acostumbrarse a algo. FAMILIAR va con WITH.

gaps.label: further afield
gaps.explanation: 'further afield' = más lejos, fuera del entorno cercano. Es fija.

gaps.label: bring back
gaps.explanation: BRING BACK = volver a traer algo, reinstaurarlo. GIVE BACK es devolver algo a su dueño.

gaps.label: keen on
gaps.explanation: 'keen ON something' = entusiasmado con algo. FOND va con OF; INTERESTED, con IN; EXCITED, con ABOUT.

title: You never get a second chance
paragraphs: It {takes} us less than a second to {form} an opinion of someone we have just met. In one well-known study, volunteers were shown photographs of strangers for just a tenth of a second. When they were given more time, they rarely {changed} their minds.

Once we have {made} up our minds about a person, we tend to notice only the information that supports our view and pay {little} attention to anything else. Psychologists call this 'confirmation bias', and it explains why it is so hard to {recover} from a bad first meeting.

There is good news, {however}. First impressions are not completely {out} of our control. Smiling, making eye {contact} and using someone's name all make a positive difference. Most importantly, experts {urge} us to give others a second chance, because, after {all}, they might be judging us just as quickly.

gaps.label: it takes (someone) + tiempo
gaps.explanation: 'it takes someone + tiempo + to do' = a alguien le lleva tanto tiempo hacer algo.

gaps.label: form an opinion
gaps.explanation: 'form an opinion' = formarse una opinión. Es la colocación estándar.

gaps.label: change your mind
gaps.explanation: 'change your mind' = cambiar de opinión. Es fija: no admite otro verbo.

gaps.label: make up your mind
gaps.explanation: 'make up your mind' = decidirse. Siempre con MAKE.

gaps.label: little vs few
gaps.explanation: ATTENTION es incontable: va con LITTLE. FEW es para contables ('few people').

gaps.label: recover from
gaps.explanation: RECOVER FROM = recuperarse de algo. CURE, RESTORE y REPAIR necesitan objeto y no llevan FROM.

gaps.label: however (al final)
gaps.explanation: HOWEVER puede cerrar la oración, entre comas. ALTHOUGH, WHEREAS y UNLESS necesitan una oración después.

gaps.label: out of control
gaps.explanation: 'out of (our) control' = fuera de nuestro control. Es fija.

gaps.label: make eye contact
gaps.explanation: 'make eye contact' = mirar a los ojos. Es fija.

gaps.label: urge someone to
gaps.explanation: URGE SOMEONE TO do = instar a alguien a algo. SUGGEST nunca lleva 'someone to': se dice 'suggest giving' o 'suggest that we give'.

gaps.label: after all
gaps.explanation: AFTER ALL = al fin y al cabo; introduce una razón que hay que tener en cuenta.

title: Scooter wars
paragraphs: Five years ago, electric scooters were almost unknown in our city. Today, you can hardly walk down a street without {coming} across one. Supporters say they are a cheap and {convenient} way to get around, and that they help to {take} cars off the road.

However, not everyone is {in} favour. Many pedestrians regularly complain {about} scooters being left on pavements, and several serious accidents have {raised} concerns about safety. Some cities have even {cracked} down on the companies that rent them out.

The real issue, experts say, is that our streets were not designed with scooters in {mind}. Until our cities finally {make} room for them, scooters will {continue} to cause conflict between those on wheels and those {on} foot.

gaps.label: come across
gaps.explanation: COME ACROSS = encontrarse con algo por casualidad.

gaps.label: convenient
gaps.explanation: CONVENIENT = práctico, cómodo. ACTUAL es 'real' y EVENTUAL es 'final': dos falsos amigos.

gaps.label: take something off the road
gaps.explanation: 'take cars off the road' = sacar autos de circulación.

gaps.label: in favour
gaps.explanation: 'be IN favour (of)' = estar a favor.

gaps.label: complain about
gaps.explanation: 'complain ABOUT something' = quejarse de algo.

gaps.label: raise concerns
gaps.explanation: RAISE es transitivo: 'raise concerns'. RISE y ARISE no llevan objeto.

gaps.label: crack down on
gaps.explanation: CRACK DOWN ON = tomar medidas duras contra algo.

gaps.label: with something in mind
gaps.explanation: 'with X in mind' = pensando en X.

gaps.label: make room for
gaps.explanation: 'make room for' = hacer lugar para.

gaps.label: continue to
gaps.explanation: CONTINUE TO + infinitivo. KEEP va con -ing ('keep causing'), y CARRY necesita ON.

gaps.label: on foot
gaps.explanation: 'ON foot' = a pie.

title: Never too old to play
paragraphs: Many adults {regret} giving up music lessons when they were children. The good news is that it is never too late to {pick} up an instrument again. Although children may learn faster, adults have one big {advantage}: they actually want to learn.

The key is to {set} realistic goals. Practising for fifteen minutes every day is far more {effective} than playing for two hours once a week. It also helps to {join} a band or a choir, where you can {make} friends with people who share your interest.

Of course, progress can be slow, and many people {feel} like giving up after a few months. When that happens, it is worth {reminding} yourself why you started. After all, the aim is not to become famous, but to {enjoy} yourself and, at the same time, to {keep} your brain active.

gaps.label: regret + -ing
gaps.explanation: REGRET + -ing = arrepentirse de haber hecho algo.

gaps.label: pick up
gaps.explanation: PICK UP = retomar o empezar algo (un instrumento, un idioma).

gaps.label: advantage
gaps.explanation: ADVANTAGE = ventaja. PROFIT es ganancia económica.

gaps.label: set goals
gaps.explanation: 'set goals' = fijarse metas.

gaps.label: effective
gaps.explanation: EFFECTIVE = eficaz, que funciona. AFFECTIVE es emocional.

gaps.label: join a group
gaps.explanation: JOIN = unirse a. PARTICIPATE necesita IN y BELONG necesita TO. ASSIST es ayudar: falso amigo.

gaps.label: make friends
gaps.explanation: 'make friends' = hacerse amigos.

gaps.label: feel like + -ing
gaps.explanation: FEEL LIKE + -ing = tener ganas de.

gaps.label: remind yourself
gaps.explanation: REMIND yourself = recordarte a vos mismo. REMEMBER no lleva un objeto reflexivo así.

gaps.label: enjoy yourself
gaps.explanation: 'enjoy yourself' = pasarla bien. FUN es sustantivo: 'have fun', sin 'yourself'.

gaps.label: keep + objeto + adjetivo
gaps.explanation: KEEP something ACTIVE = mantener algo activo. STAY y REMAIN no llevan objeto.

title: The multitasking myth
paragraphs: Many of us {pride} ourselves on being able to do several things at once. We answer emails during meetings, {check} our phones while watching films, and believe we are getting more {done}.

Research, however, {tells} a very different story. The brain cannot really concentrate {on} two demanding tasks at the same time. Instead, it switches rapidly between them, and every switch {comes} at a cost. One study found that people who were constantly interrupted made twice as many mistakes {as} those who were left alone.

The solution is simple, though not easy: do one thing {at} a time. Turn off notifications, {set} aside specific times for checking messages, and {resist} the temptation to look at your phone. You may be surprised by how much more you {achieve}.

gaps.label: pride yourself on
gaps.explanation: PRIDE YOURSELF ON = enorgullecerse de.

gaps.label: check
gaps.explanation: CHECK = revisar, mirar. CONTROL es controlar, dominar: falso amigo.

gaps.label: get things done
gaps.explanation: 'get things done' = sacar cosas adelante.

gaps.label: tell a story
gaps.explanation: 'tell a (different) story' = contar otra historia. Con 'story' va TELL, no SAY.

gaps.label: concentrate on
gaps.explanation: 'concentrate ON' = concentrarse en.

gaps.label: come at a cost
gaps.explanation: 'come at a cost' = tener un precio.

gaps.label: twice as many … as
gaps.explanation: 'twice AS many … AS' = el doble que. No va THAN: es una comparación de igualdad multiplicada.

gaps.label: one at a time
gaps.explanation: 'one thing AT a time' = una cosa por vez.

gaps.label: set aside
gaps.explanation: SET ASIDE = reservar (tiempo, dinero).

gaps.label: resist the temptation
gaps.explanation: 'resist the temptation' = resistir la tentación.

gaps.label: achieve
gaps.explanation: ACHIEVE = lograr. REACH necesita una meta concreta; SUCCEED va con IN.

title: The cinema that refused to die
paragraphs: When our town's only cinema announced it was going to close {down}, a group of residents decided to {take} action. Within a week, they had {set} up a website asking for donations, and the response was {beyond} their wildest dreams.

In just two months, they {raised} enough money to buy the building. Volunteers now {run} the cinema, and tickets cost {less} than half the price of a big multiplex. The programme {includes} everything from classic films to new releases.

The cinema has become much more than a place to watch films. It is now the {heart} of the community, hosting quiz nights, school concerts and even weddings. 'We never expected it to be such a {success},' says one of the organisers. 'It just {goes} to show what people can do when they work together.'

gaps.label: close down
gaps.explanation: CLOSE DOWN = cerrar definitivamente un negocio.

gaps.label: take action
gaps.explanation: 'take action' = tomar medidas.

gaps.label: set up
gaps.explanation: SET UP = crear, armar (una web, una empresa).

gaps.label: beyond your wildest dreams
gaps.explanation: 'beyond their wildest dreams' = más allá de lo que soñaban.

gaps.label: raise money
gaps.explanation: 'raise money' = juntar dinero. RAISE es transitivo; ROSE es el pasado de RISE, que no lleva objeto.

gaps.label: run a business
gaps.explanation: RUN = dirigir, hacer funcionar (un negocio, un cine).

gaps.label: cost less than
gaps.explanation: 'cost LESS than' = costar menos que. FEWER es para sustantivos contables.

gaps.label: include
gaps.explanation: INCLUDE = incluir, con objeto directo. CONSIST necesita OF.

gaps.label: the heart of the community
gaps.explanation: 'the heart of' = el centro, lo más vital de algo.

gaps.label: such a success
gaps.explanation: 'such a success' = un éxito tan grande. SUCCEED es verbo.

gaps.label: it goes to show
gaps.explanation: 'it (just) goes to show' = eso demuestra.

title: Why we buy what we don't need
paragraphs: Most of us have, at some point, {given} in to the temptation to buy something we did not need. Advertisers know exactly how to {take} advantage of our weaknesses, and they are very good {at} it. Limited-time offers, for {instance}, create a sense of urgency that makes us act without thinking.

Psychologists also {point} out that shopping can be a way of dealing with stress. Buying something new gives us a pleasant feeling, but it soon {wears} off, and we are left {with} more things and less money.

So how can we {break} the habit? One simple but useful {piece} of advice is to wait 48 hours before buying anything that is not essential. In most {cases}, the desire simply disappears. Another is to ask yourself whether you would still want the item if it were not {on} sale.

title: Not just feeding the lions
paragraphs: Most people think zookeepers spend their days playing with animals, but nothing could be {further} from the truth. My day begins at six, when I {carry} out a health check on every animal in my {care}.

Then comes the least glamorous part of the job: cleaning enclosures, which {takes} a lot of energy. Feeding time is the {highlight} of my day, but it is far from simple. Some animals are fed {according} to strict timetables, and we have to keep a {close} eye on their weight.

The job can be physically {demanding}, and the pay is not great. But for me, there is nothing {quite} like the moment when an animal I have looked {after} for years recognises me. I wouldn't change it for the {world}.

title: Nothing is really free
paragraphs: Most of the apps on our phones cost nothing to download. But, as the saying goes, there is no {such} thing as a free lunch. In {exchange} for using them, we give away information about ourselves: where we go, what we buy and even who we {spend} time with.
This data is {worth} a fortune to advertisers, who can then {target} us with ads. Most users {agree} to this without realising it, because very few people {bother} to read the terms and conditions.

Experts are not saying that we should {give} up our phones. But they do recommend {checking} which permissions each app asks for and {turning} off location tracking when it is not needed. After all, if you are not paying for the product, there is a good {chance} that you are the product.
